title: Foundations: Funk Rock - The Complete Guide
summary: What Funk Rock is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Funk Rock songs: Funk is rhythm as religion: the One, the syncopated bass, the chicken-scratch guitar, and horns hitting like punctuation. James Brown invented it; Parliament-Funkadelic took it to the mothership.

History: James Brown's mid-1960s breakthrough (Papa's Got a Brand New Bag, 1965; Cold Sweat, 1967) shifted the accent to beat one. Sly Stone, Parliament-Funkadelic, and Prince carried funk through the 1970s–80s.

How the songs work: Funk Rock favors the keys of E, G, A, D. Common forms include Extended vamps with breakdowns; Call-and-response between band sections. Players should master the one: everything lands on beat one first, then chicken-scratch guitar: muted 16ths. Groove keys; no capos.

title: Funk Rock Etude No. 1: P-Funk i–VII–VI
summary: An original Funk Rock study in G drilling chicken-scratch guitar: muted 16ths.
body:
This original etude isolates the 'P-Funk i–VII–VI' progression in the key of G — the changes Funk Rock players must know cold.

CHART:
Gm7 | F7 | D#7 | D7

FORM: call-and-response between band sections.

PRACTICE: loop the chart slowly, adding chicken-scratch guitar: muted 16ths once the changes are clean. Then transpose with the included program and drill it in all twelve keys — the Funk Rock player's rite of passage.

title: Cold Sweat - Funk Rock Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Cold Sweat by James Brown (1967).
body:
Cold Sweat — James Brown, 1967. The funk big bang: the One is born.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of A):
A7 | D7 | A7 | A7

This study chart uses the 'Sly I–IV–vamp' progression, the Funk Rock workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: extended vamps with breakdowns. Listen for bass as lead instrument (bootsy, larry graham) — it is the fingerprint of the style.

TO PLAY IT: set your tempo to the Funk Rock pocket, voice the chords cleanly, and let bass as lead instrument (bootsy, larry graham). Groove keys; no capos. (Song facts: title/artist/year are documented public records; the chart is an original study arrangement.)
